deals.headline: Harris and Blitzer buy a majority stake in the Devils, with the right to operate Prudential Center
deals.investor: Josh Harris and David Blitzer (later HBSE)
deals.summary: In August 2013 Josh Harris and David Blitzer bought a majority stake in the Devils, including the rights to operate the Prudential Center (HBSE). Forbes lists the price paid as $320M.

deals.date_text: Reported May 2026 (stake held via two holding companies; date of investment not stated)
deals.evidence: Arctos owns roughly 15% of HBSE via a pair of holding companies
deals.headline: Arctos holds roughly 15% of HBSE, parent of the Devils
deals.summary: Sportico reports Arctos has invested in Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment; an internal WNBA expansion memo indicated Arctos owns roughly 15% of HBSE via a pair of holding companies. The stake is in HBSE, not directly in the Devils.

name: New Jersey Devils
notes: Franchise founded 1974 as the Kansas City Scouts (NHL records API first season 1974-75); the club's own history page says the New Jersey Devils organisation began in 1982 after relocating via Colorado. Revenue/operating income/player costs are Forbes estimates (Dec 2025, 2024-25 season); Forbes value $2.4B, debt/value 5%, gate receipts $78M. Valuation is Sportico's 29 Sep 2026 list ($2.72bn, figures in USD millions in the data file). Prudential Center is reported elsewhere as owned by the Newark Housing Authority and operated by HBSE, but no citable page stating it was read, so stadium_owner is null; NJ lawmakers approved a $300M tax incentive for an arena redevelopment in Jan 2026 (NJ Spotlight page could not be loaded to verify). Arctos's ~15% is in HBSE (parent), not a stated Devils stake. GM is Sunny Mehta (staff directory); Bob Myers is president of HBSE Sports (Oct 2025). Arena capacity evidence is in the 2025-26 media guide PDF (organisational directory, 'Seating Capacity 16,514'). No legal entity, attendance, sponsor or social counts found on citable pages.

ownership_summary: Owned since August 2013 by Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment (HBSE), led by managing partners Josh Harris and David Blitzer, with limited partners including David Adelman, Martin Geller and Marc Leder; HBSE also holds the rights to operate the Prudential Center. Arctos owns roughly 15% of HBSE through two holding companies, per a WNBA expansion memo reported by Sportico.
